transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since the car crash, it’s like the accident keeps replaying in my head when I’m awake and when I’m trying to relax, and I can’t shut it off. It just feels like I'm constantly stuck in that moment and I don't know how to make it stop.
Do you experience any other symptoms like avoiding places or people that remind you of the crash, or feeling overly alert or easily startled?

Yeah, I definitely do—I make excuses to avoid driving and won't go anywhere near that intersection, and I'll shut down or change the subject if anyone brings it up. I also feel constantly on edge and tense in my chest, like I'm waiting for something bad to happen even when I'm just sitting at my desk or at church.

Can you tell me more about what you experience when you're in a situation that reminds you of the crash, such as the intersection where it happened, and how that affects your daily life and relationships?

I completely avoid that intersection and make excuses to my family so I don't have to get in a car at all, and I shut down if anyone brings up the crash. Because of this, I've been bailing on weekend plans and skipping my church groups. I'm just pulling away from my friends because I can't handle being around people or near cars right now.
Can you describe how your feeling of being 'on edge' and 'waiting for something bad to happen' affects your ability to sleep or concentrate on daily tasks?

That constant tension makes it impossible to wind down at night, so I just stare at the ceiling for hours and constantly jerk awake from half-dreams of screeching brakes. During the day, that exhaustion makes it so hard to concentrate that I zone out on customer calls, which has gotten me written up and forces me to step away from my desk.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself, or like the world around you isn't real, especially when you're reminded of the car crash or feeling overwhelmed?

No, I don't really feel like I'm outside of my body or like the world around me isn't real, even when I'm completely overwhelmed. Everything still feels very real to me—honestly, sometimes it feels a little too real.

You mentioned you don't feel like you're outside of your body or that the world isn't real, but can you tell me if you've experienced any feelings of numbness or detachment from others or yourself since the car crash?

I don't really feel numb or detached from myself, but I definitely feel disconnected from the people around me. I've been shutting down and bailing on church groups and weekend plans with my friends because I just can't handle being around people or talking about what happened.
Can you describe if there are any specific emotions that you feel you've lost touch with or have difficulty experiencing since the car crash, such as happiness, love, or excitement?

I'm not really sure about that, and I haven't thought about it that way. Mostly, I just feel completely overwhelmed by this constant mix of tension and guilt in my chest, so there doesn't seem to be room for much else.
Can you think of any activities or things that used to bring you joy or excitement before the car crash, and if so, do you still find pleasure in them now?

I used to love going for early-morning runs, hiking with my friends on weekends, and being really active in my church group. But I don't do any of that anymore or find pleasure in them, since I avoid driving to the hikes and feel too on edge to handle being around people at church. I've just been bailing on all of it because of how I feel.

You've mentioned not feeling outside of your body or the world being unreal, but can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling 'completely stuck in that moment' of the car crash, and does that feel like a kind of reliving the event or more like a memory that you can't get out of your head?

It definitely feels like I'm actually reliving it, not just having a bad memory. When a customer raises their voice or I hear tires on the wet road outside, I feel like I'm physically back in that smashed car hearing the metal crunching and my friend gasping. It's like I'm right there in that exact moment again and I can't make it stop.
